nodes.name: Hourly Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 12 h. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Read Source Feed
nodes.notes: Pulls the RSS feed and emits one item per entry (title, link, content). Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Skip Already-Seen Posts
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Keep Top Stories
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 5 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
nodes.notes: Single fixed LLM step (no tool choice) — cheaper and more predictable than an agent. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Google Gemini Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: models/gemini-2.5-flash). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: Google AI API key. aistudio.google.com/apikey → Create API key.

nodes.name: Publish to Twilio
nodes.notes: Sends an SMS via Twilio — reserved for urgent alerts since SMS costs money per message, unlike chat notifications. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Twilio SID + token. Twilio Console → Account Info → Account SID + Auth Token.

nodes.name: Publish to Slack
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#social) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Confirm Cross-Post
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Log Published Posts (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Post Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per post (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Post Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Post Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 50 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Sort Posts Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty content
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Listen for keywords with Google Sheets & Twilio

**Pattern:** Social Listening · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers engagement work end to end across Google Sheets, Twilio, Notion and Slack.

It moves through 30 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Read Source Feed
3. Skip Already-Seen Posts
4. Keep Top Stories
5. Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
6. Google Gemini Chat Model
7. Publish to Twilio
8. Publish to Slack
9. Confirm Cross-Post
10. Log Published Posts (Google Sheets)
11. Fingerprint for Idempotency
12. Drop Already-Processed Items
13. Enrich with Reference Data
14. Fold In Enrichment Fields
15. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
16. Archive Row Snapshot
17. Load Previous Snapshot
18. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
19. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
20. Record Sub-workflow Result
21. Stamp Completion Time
22. Persist Run Metadata
23. Align Field Names
24. Save Execution Metadata
25. Cap Batch Volume
26. Sort Posts Newest First
27. Guard Non-Empty content
28. Summarize Run Stats
29. Append Audit Row (Notion)
30. Send Summary to Twilio

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing engagement work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Read Source Feed → Skip Already-Seen Posts → Keep Top Stories → Rewrite for Our Audience (AI) → Google Gemini Chat Model → Publish to Twilio → Publish to Slack → Confirm Cross-Post → Log Published Posts (Google Sheets) → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Align Field Names → Save Execution Metadata → Cap Batch Volume → Sort Posts Newest First → Guard Non-Empty content → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Twilio → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Twilio aligned by hand for engagement
- Engagement work where "Read Source Feed" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Engagement work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Twilio in step for engagement, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Twilio are skipped, across all 33 nodes of this engagement build
- A failed Google Sheets or Twilio call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 33 nodes in this engagement build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a engagement run reports once rather than 33 times
- Every engagement run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google AI API key; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2; Twilio SID + token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Deduplication is cross-execution, not just within a single run — an RSS feed re-serves the same items on every poll, and without this the same story would get posted again on every scheduled check.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Turn off the AI rewrite step and compare the raw feed text against the rewritten version.
2. Add a second RSS source and merge both into one feed before dedupe.
3. Change 'Keep Top Stories' from 5 to 1 and see how it changes posting cadence.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google AI API key**
aistudio.google.com/apikey → Create API key.
_Gotcha:_ Free tier is rate-limited per minute.

**Twilio SID + token**
Twilio Console → Account Info → Account SID + Auth Token.
_Gotcha:_ The `from` number must be one you own in Twilio. Trial accounts only send to verified numbers.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your engagement process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Twilio: an API key/secret pair scoped to messaging, not the account SID and auth token.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole engagement payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
